rejected.title: Refugees from Vietnam
card: The Vietnam War ended in 1975 when communist forces took over South Vietnam. Many people who had supported the old government, or who feared the new one, fled the country.

A refugee is a person who flees their country because of a well-founded fear of harm, and cannot safely return. Many Vietnamese refugees left in small, crowded boats, and some waited in refugee camps in nearby countries.
The first boats reached northern Australia in 1976. Over the following years, tens of thousands of Vietnamese people were accepted, some by boat and many more through organised resettlement programs.

Their arrival tested Australian attitudes. Some people welcomed them and some feared them. Over time, Vietnamese Australians built communities, businesses and public lives, and many Australians came to see refugee resettlement as part of the nation's story.
rejected.remember: Vietnamese refugees fled after 1975, some by boat, and their arrival tested attitudes and then helped change them.

a.q: Why did many Vietnamese people leave their country after 1975?
opts: They feared harm under the new government
They were invited to fill jobs in Australia
They were sent by the Australian government
They wanted to join the Snowy Mountains work
a.why: Many people who had backed the old government, or feared the new one, fled for safety. That makes them refugees, not workers recruited by Australia. The Snowy Mountains Scheme was an earlier project and had nothing to do with their leaving.
a.clue: Think about the meaning of the word refugee.

b.q: In 1980, some Australians feared the Vietnamese arrivals, but by 2000 many Vietnamese Australians ran businesses and joined public life. What does this show about their arrival?
opts: It tested attitudes, which then changed over time
It ended all debate about refugees in Australia
It showed that attitudes stayed the same over time
It showed that few refugees settled in Australia
b.why: Early fear and later acceptance show attitudes tested and then changing, as the card describes. The debate did not end, and the growth of communities shows many refugees did settle. Attitudes did not stay the same.
b.clue: Compare the mood in 1980 with the mood in 2000.

version.title: Refugees from Vietnam
card: The Vietnam War ended in 1975 when communist North Vietnam took over South Vietnam. Many people linked to the old government, or afraid of the new one, fled.

a person who flees their country because of a real fear of harm and cannot safely go back. Many Vietnamese escaped in small, crowded boats, and many waited in camps in nearby countries such as Malaysia and Thailand.
The first boat reached Darwin in 1976. About 2,000 people came straight to Australia by boat, but far more were chosen from the camps and flown here, tens of thousands by the mid-1980s.

Their arrival tested Australians' attitudes: some feared them, while the government and many others welcomed them. As Vietnamese Australians built communities and businesses, such as in Footscray and Springvale, more Australians came to accept them.
version.remember: Most Vietnamese refugees came from camps, some by boat. Early fears gave way to wider acceptance as their communities grew.

a.q: What made many of the Vietnamese who left after 1975 refugees?
opts: They fled a real fear of harm and could not go back
They wanted higher pay and a better life abroad
They were chosen to fill jobs Australia needed
They reached another country by boat, not plane
a.why: A refugee flees a real fear of harm and cannot safely return, as many did after the communist takeover. Wanting higher pay makes someone a migrant, not a refugee. Travelling by boat does not decide it: most were flown to Australia from camps.
a.clue: Think about why they left, not how they travelled.

b.q: A 1977 letter to a newspaper warns about refugee boats. In 1995 the Vietnamese shops and restaurants of a Melbourne suburb are popular with locals. What do the two sources suggest?
opts: Attitudes were tested, then changed over time
Attitudes stayed fearful even as communities grew
Most refugees came by boat and settled in Darwin
Australians welcomed the refugees from the very start
b.why: The letter shows early fear, and the busy shops show a community that grew and was accepted, so attitudes were tested and then changed. They were not welcomed by everyone from the start, and the popular shops show fear did not stay the same.
b.clue: Compare the mood in 1977 with the mood in 1995.

a.best: They fled a real fear of harm and could not go back

b.best: Attitudes were tested, then changed over time
